newsitem.title: USA: California retail diesel, gasoline prices fall.
newsitem.headline: California retail diesel, gasoline prices fall.

text.p: Retail prices for diesel fuel in California fell slightly this week amid rising supplies, according to the California Energy Commission (CEC).
The price of unleaded gasoline sold at service stations also fell as inventories increased and wholesale prices continued their half-month slide.
West Coast supplies of gasoline rose by 520,000 barrels to 30.2 million barrels as of June 6, according to trade industry data.
Pressure also came from spot wholesale prices, which have fallen about seven cents a gallon from the beginning of June
As of June 9, the average retail price for state-mandated (CARB) gasoline was $1.33 a gallon, down one cent from a week earlier, the CEC said.
The average price of diesel fuel also fell one cent to $1.30 a gallon.
Retail diesel fuel was highest in northern California, where prices averaged $1.34 a barrel. Southern California diesel fuel averaged $1.33 a gallon and the central region stood at $1.25 a gallon.
CEC did not provide regional breakdowns for gasoline prices, but will soon.
